content:
Chris Christie thinks “people are misreading” Donald Trump’s decision to replace Susie Wiles with hard-liner Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff following the GOP’s rout in the 2026 midterm elections.

“This decision by Trump shows his level of fear and insecurity right now,” the former New Jersey governor and two-time GOP presidential candidate told Rolling Stone’s Matt Bai in a lengthy interview published Tuesday.

The president “picked the only person around him who’s been there from the beginning, a person who he knows is undyingly loyal, won’t leak on him, won’t countermand any of his instructions,” said Christie, a onetime, longtime friend of Trump who’s now a fierce critic of him.

Then he added: “Stephen Miller is comfort food for Donald Trump in a moment of crisis. He’s his teddy bear to bring to bed because he’s scared.”

Bai suggested it was “a very disturbing image.”

“And meant to be so,” replied Christie, who elsewhere in the interview confirmed he was considering a third run for the White House in 2028 and predicted it would “take a few months” for Trump “to get his feet back underneath him” following Republicans’ bruising defeat earlier this month.

“He’s defeated. He’s lost his compass a little bit,” Christie said of Trump.

But he warned: “He’ll get it back. And I think that we’ll see a really angry last couple of years.”

Christie pointed to two reasons: The Democrats poised to take control of Congress “will make him really angry” with their oversight of his administration and “because the attention will start to be shifted to someone else.”

Trump “needs attention like you and I need oxygen,” said Christie.

“And when they start focusing on the Republican and Democratic primaries for president, and he’s not the center of attention, he’s not out of the picture, but he is now sharing the stage with others,” he added. “That will be very difficult for him. And what he’ll do is to try to act even more outrageously, so that you have to turn the camera back to him exclusively.”
